newsitem.title: FRANCE: RUGBY UNION-FRANCE NAME REVAMPED TEAM FOR GRAND SLAM DECIDER.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-FRANCE NAME REVAMPED TEAM FOR GRAND SLAM DECIDER.

text.p: Injuries once again forced the French selectors to reshuffle their team ahead of Saturday's Five Nations' grand slam decider against Scotland at Parc des Princes.
France, who have been without several key players in all their matches so far in the tournament, lost both their half-backs and one prop since beating England 23-20 at Twickenham on March 1.

Pau fly-half David Aucagne takes over from the injured Alain Penaud while Guy Accoceberry replaces Penaud's Brive team mate Philippe Carbonneau at scrum-half in the side announced on Wednesday by coach Jean-Claude Skrela.
Penaud has a pulled thigh muscle while first-choice number nine Carbonneau is recovering from a twisted ankle and will start as a substitute.
Brive prop Didier Casadei wins his first cap in place of Christian Califano, who was automatically suspended after being sent off for punching an opponent in a league game at the weekend.
"Casadei has proved that he had international class by helping Brive win the European Cup," said Skrela. "He's the same type of player as Califano and he should fit in without any problems."
Aucagne, a useful replacement in the team who beat Wales last February, is a dynamic fly-half with taste for fluent, open rugby.
"Against Wales, he did just what he expected him to do and he certainly deserved another chance," Skrela said.
Accoceberry, the logical solution at scrum-half when Carbonneau is not available, said he knew what was at stake.
"A grand slam does not happen often in a player's career," he said, knowing that France have achieved only four in their history and have not completed one since 1987.
"It's something that stays, people remember it and still talk about it years after."
Casadei was in a similar frame of mind: "Its' a great opportunity we can't afford to miss," he said.
The morale was high in the rural retreat outside Paris where France prepare for key internationals despite the absence of Penaud, who was close to tears when he left the training camp on Tuesday.
"We all felt sorry for him", said Aucagne. "But it is our duty to focus on the match. We want to win it badly."
French manager Jo Maso said it would be a costly mistake to underrate Scotland, who won their last two Five Nations encounters with France.
"We must not think that we have done the hardest part by beating England," he said. "Scotland are a strong side and they will have nothing to lose. We must be ready for a tough fight."

Team - 15-Jean-Luc Sadourny; 14-Laurent Leflamand, 13-Christophe Lamaison, 12-Stephane Glas, 11-David Venditti; 10-David Aucagne, 9-Guy Accoceberry; 8-Fabien Pelous, 7-Olivier Magne, 6-Abdelatif Benazzi (captain), 5-Hugues Miorin, 4-Olivier Merle, 3-Franck Tournaire, 2-Marc Dal Maso, 1-Didier Casadei.
Substitutes - 16-Pierre Bonduy, 17-Ugo Mola, 18-Philippe Carbonneau, 19-Richard Castel, 20-Jean-Louis Jordana, 21-Marc de Rougemont.
